findings.description: The security group allows inbound TCP/22 from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing SSH on a publicly addressable instance to the entire internet and enabling brute-force or exploit attempts against the management port.

findings.issue_category: Unrestricted HTTP ingress and cleartext transport
findings.description: Inbound TCP/80 is open to 0.0.0.0/0 and the instance serves plain HTTP (Apache with no TLS), so all portal traffic is transmitted in cleartext over the public internet.
The egress rule permits all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0, providing no outbound segmentation and allowing a compromised instance unrestricted command-and-control or data-exfiltration paths.

The user_data script exports AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY literals. EC2 user data is retrievable from the instance metadata service by any process or SSRF on the host and is stored unencrypted in the instance description, leaking long-lived IAM credentials.

No metadata_options block is set, so the instance defaults to allowing IMDSv1 (http_tokens optional). Combined with a publicly reachable web server, this makes credential theft via SSRF against 169.254.169.254 trivial.
No root_block_device with encrypted = true is specified, so the instance root EBS volume may be created unencrypted, leaving data at rest unprotected.

The instance is launched into a subnet with map_public_ip_on_launch enabled and a default route to an internet gateway, so it receives a public IP and is directly reachable from the internet with no load balancer, NAT, or bastion boundary.
The EBS data volume attached to the portal server does not set encrypted = true or a kms_key_id, so its contents are stored unencrypted.
The snapshot is taken from an unencrypted EBS volume, so the backup copy of the data is also stored unencrypted and inherits no KMS protection.
The VPC flow log destination bucket defines no server-side encryption configuration, so network telemetry that can reveal internal topology and traffic patterns is stored without enforced encryption.

findings.issue_category: No public access block or ACL controls
findings.description: The bucket has no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block, ownership controls, or private ACL declared, leaving it dependent on account defaults and vulnerable to accidental public exposure of flow log data.
No bucket policy enforces aws:SecureTransport, so flow log objects may be read or written over unencrypted HTTP connections.
The bucket storing VPC flow logs has force_destroy = true and no versioning or object lock, so security audit evidence can be deleted or overwritten by an attacker or an accidental terraform destroy.
map_public_ip_on_launch = true causes every instance in this subnet to receive a public IP address, removing network segmentation and exposing workloads directly to the internet by default.
map_public_ip_on_launch = true causes every instance in this subnet to receive a public IP address, removing network segmentation and exposing workloads directly to the internet by default.

The VPC does not manage its default security group (no aws_default_security_group restricting all rules), so any resource launched without an explicit group inherits the default group's permissive intra-group behaviour rather than an explicitly denied one.
